title: Technology
subtitle: Shaping a better future
lead: How digital tools change the way students learn, teachers teach and communities share information. A mixed-methods study with 420 survey respondents and 24 interviews in three Indonesian cities.

footer.text: Faculty of Computer Science, Universitas Nusantara  |  research@example.ac.id  |  www.example.ac.id

sections.title: Abstract
sections.text: This study examines how technology adoption affects learning outcomes, teaching practice and civic participation. We combine a survey of 420 respondents with 24 interviews and a document analysis of school policies. Adoption is high but uneven: access is no longer the main barrier, skills and support are.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.text: Since 2020 every school in the sample has an internet connection, yet only 41% of teachers use digital tools weekly. This gap between access and use is the starting point of the study.

items.title: 1. Research
items.text: Students with weekly device use score 12% higher in reading tests

items.title: 2. Communication
items.text: Teachers who join online communities adopt new tools twice as fast

items.title: 3. Challenges
items.text: Skills and technical support, not connectivity, limit adoption

sections.title: Research Questions
items: How does device use relate to learning outcomes?
What support do schools need most?
How do communities use school technology?

items.label: Time saved

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.text: Investment should move from hardware to training and support.

items.title: For students
items.text: Weekly guided practice with digital tools, not only free access

items.title: For educators
items.text: Peer communities and paid time for training

items.title: For society
items.text: Open school labs after hours for parents and neighbours

items.title: For government
items.text: Fund technical support staff, one per five schools
